en: One milliliter of liquid water expands to approximately 1,700 milliliters of steam when boiled at 100 degrees Celsius.
Osmium is the densest natural element at 22.59 grams per cubic centimeter, making it exactly twice as dense as lead.
At 20 degrees Celsius, a maximum of 360 grams of table salt can dissolve in one single liter of water.
Heating 168 grams of baking soda produces exactly 106 grams of solid sodium carbonate, releasing 62 grams of water vapor and carbon dioxide.
Tungsten has the highest melting point of all metals, remaining completely solid until it reaches a scorching 3,422 degrees Celsius.
On the Mohs hardness scale, diamond is the hardest natural mineral at 10, while talc is the softest at 1.
When liquid water freezes into solid ice, it expands by about 9 percent in volume, making ice less dense than water.
Earth's atmosphere is a gas mixture containing roughly 78 percent nitrogen, 21 percent oxygen, and 1 percent other trace gases.
Liquid helium has the lowest boiling point of any element, turning into a gas at a freezing minus 268.9 degrees Celsius.
Sound travels through solid steel at 5,960 meters per second, which is roughly 17 times faster than it travels through air.
Over 99 percent of the visible universe is made of plasma, making it the most common state of matter in space.
Human blood plasma is a liquid solution containing about 92 percent water, 7 percent proteins, and 1 percent dissolved salts.
